summary.one_liner: A Chef cookbook, marked deprecated and no longer supported, meant to set up a default, hardened Jenkins server behind nginx with SSL and user login configuration.
summary.what_it_does: The cookbook describes itself as aiming to provide a secure default Jenkins setup. It says it installs Jenkins behind nginx, configures SSL for nginx, configures user logins, and runs Jenkins slaves on different servers. It installs a default plugin list (for example ant, git-client, github, matrix-auth, maven-plugin, rvm, swarm, and windows-slaves), which can be overridden through a node attribute. It has a Windows slaves section, but the README gives no details under it. The README says it is designed to be used with chef-os-hardening and chef-ssh-hardening, though it has no direct dependency on them. Testing uses Bundler, a rake lint task, and Test Kitchen.
use_cases: hardening a Jenkins CI server with Chef
running Jenkins behind an nginx SSL proxy
deploying Jenkins slaves on separate servers
managing Jenkins plugins through Chef attributes
notable: Deprecated and no longer supported, according to the README
Installs Jenkins behind nginx with SSL configured
Default plugin list can be overridden via node attributes
Intended to pair with chef-os-hardening and chef-ssh-hardening
Part of the Deutsche Telekom dev-sec hardening project family
caveats: Deprecated and no longer supported; the README invites contacting the maintainers to discuss support
The README says it is a work in progress and not yet secure enough for production use
The Test section names only the ubuntu-1204 Kitchen platform, which is old
